//: Budgets for scripts/perf-report.mjs. Every number under `bundle` was measured on this repository with `npm run build` and then given 5% headroom on a size or one whole unit on a count; none of them is a round number somebody liked the look of. Regenerate with `npm run perf:report -- --update-budgets` and read the diff — a budget that moves up is a decision, not a formality. Numbers under `runtime` are null until someone runs `npm run perf:runtime -- <origin>` with `--update-budgets` against a server they started; a null budget reports as `uncalibrated` and warns, and is never treated as a pass.
measuredAgainst: commit 51dc373, Next.js 16.3.2 Turbopack production build, gzip -9
//route_css_gz_kb: Re-baselined 2026-09-03 from 40.2 after the CLEAN-008 pass, and the rise is not a regression. Deleting ~11 kB of provably unreachable CSS moved this metric from 38.3 to 42.8: Turbopack packs shared CSS into ~120 kB buckets shipped to every route, and removing rules moved the bucket boundary so archive.module.css and influence-graph.module.css fell from route-private chunks into the universal set. Total emitted CSS fell 64.9 -> 60.7 over the same change. Watch total_css_gz_kb for the cleanup work; this one is a coarse tripwire on the universal bucket set, nothing finer.
//real_finding: admin.module.css (23.9 kB), archive.module.css (34.2 kB) and visualizer.module.css (34.6 kB) ride on every public route. That is ~93 kB of source CSS the reading routes never use, and it is worth far more than either tripwire. It is Turbopack's client-CSS bucketing, not an import-graph defect: deep-importing the barrel consumers was tried and moved nothing.
